content.summary: Connecting energy sub-metering, indoor air quality, and predictive maintenance through IoTRICs—a facilities-management approach for Nokia HQ Dubai.
content.clientOverview:
Nokia HQ Dubai is the corporate-office setting for this smart facilities-management project. The supplied project scope brings together energy sub-metering, indoor air-quality monitoring, and predictive maintenance through IoTRICs, with LoRaWAN connectivity.

The focus is the day-to-day work of facilities management: understanding how a building uses energy, maintaining a comfortable indoor environment, and identifying where equipment needs attention.
content.challenge:
Bring the building’s signals into focus.

Corporate facilities need to balance energy use, occupant comfort, and equipment reliability. A building-wide total or an isolated sensor reading tells only part of that story. The operational question is how those measurements can support a useful decision.

The Nokia HQ Dubai project scope addresses three connected priorities: understanding energy consumption at a more detailed level, making indoor air quality visible, and supporting a more proactive approach to maintenance.

The facilities-management priorities

  • Energy visibility: move beyond a single overall consumption figure to understand the loads being monitored.
  • Indoor environments: provide context for reviewing air quality in occupied spaces.
  • Equipment attention: use monitoring information to support maintenance investigation and planning.
  • Connected information: relate readings to the facilities and assets they describe.
The aim is to make building information useful to the people responsible for its everyday operation.
content.solution:
One connected approach to smart facilities.

The project brings energy sub-metering, air-quality monitoring, and predictive maintenance into an end-to-end IoT facilities scope using IoTRICs. LoRaWAN is identified in the project brief as part of the connectivity approach.

01 / Energy sub-metering

Sub-metering gives the facilities team a more detailed view of the electrical loads being monitored. Reviewing consumption patterns can help frame questions about operating hours, changes in demand, and areas that warrant further investigation.

02 / Indoor air-quality monitoring

Air-quality monitoring adds another view of the workplace environment. Readings can be considered alongside occupancy and building operation to help the team understand when an indoor space needs closer attention.

03 / Predictive-maintenance focus

Predictive maintenance is part of the stated project scope. The emphasis is on using equipment information to inform when an asset should be investigated, rather than treating maintenance as a separate activity from monitoring.

04 / LoRaWAN connectivity

LoRaWAN provides the wireless-connectivity element named in the brief. Within a facilities-monitoring approach, connectivity links field measurements to the information used for operational review.

A practical operational workflow

  1. Identify the energy, environmental, or equipment question to be answered.
  2. Review the relevant measurements in the context of the monitored asset or space.
  3. Investigate an exception and decide whether an operational or maintenance response is needed.
  4. Record the response and continue reviewing the trend.
content.results:
Focus on the operational value.

The project’s intended value is a more connected view of facilities performance across energy, indoor air quality, and maintenance. These are the operational goals of the supplied scope; quantified post-deployment results have not been provided.

Understand consumption in context

Sub-metered information provides a starting point for investigating how monitored loads behave, including changes across operating periods.

Keep the indoor environment visible

Air-quality monitoring helps make environmental conditions part of the facilities-management conversation alongside energy and equipment performance.

Inform maintenance decisions

Equipment monitoring supports a more informed discussion about inspection priorities and the condition of monitored assets.

Build a basis for evaluation

A measured case-study update can compare an agreed baseline with verified operational data. Energy savings, response times, and maintenance improvements should be reported only when the client-approved figures and measurement periods are available.
